body.name: v2.0.0
body.message:
fix: fix issue, pull request, commit and status edge cases (#120)

`gt issue create --blocked-by/--blocking` created the issue and then failed on a missing dependency; missing issues are now refused first. Pin, unpin and unlock acted again on items already in that state; like lock and gh, they now report it and change nothing, and issue and pull request JSON gains `locked` (and `pinned` for pull requests). Merging a pull request blocked by an open dependency surfaced a bare server error; it now names the blocking issues, and `gt pr view` tells a deleted head branch or open blockers apart from conflicts. `gt pr checks --required` named the head branch instead of the base branch. `gt commit pr` printed nothing without `--json` and failed on abbreviated SHAs. `gt status --json` printed `mentions: null`. `gt pr review --pending` named the wrong flag in its body error, `gt pr review reply` checked an empty body only after a request, and `gt time cancel` asked to discard a stopwatch that was not running.

Reviewed-on: https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/120

body.name: v1.2.0
body.message:
feat: add --admin, --match-head-commit, --disable-auto, --required and --fill-first/--fill-verbose to the pr commands (#97)

`gh pr merge`, `checks` and `create` have options that `gt pr` lacked:

- `gt pr merge --admin` merges past the branch protection (Gitea's `force_merge`, for those who administer the repository). `--match-head-commit SHA` merges only while the head is still that commit and fails with the `head_mismatch` exit status otherwise, so a push after the review is not merged unseen. `--disable-auto` cancels the merge that `--auto` scheduled and merges nothing; with none scheduled it says so.
- `gt pr checks --required` shows and awaits only the checks that the protection rule of the base branch requires (`effective_branch_protection_name`, then its `status_check_contexts`, where `*` and `?` match). A flaky optional check no longer holds `--watch` back, and a branch that requires none has nothing to show.
- `gt pr create --fill-first` takes the title and body from the first commit of the branch whatever their number; `--fill-verbose` takes the body from the full message of every commit, oldest first. `--fill` is unchanged. `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose` cannot be combined, like gh.

`gh pr checks --fail-fast` is not added: `gt pr checks --watch` already stops at the first failure.

Tested against fake servers, and on the disposable Gitea 28 instance by three integration tests: a merge with a moved head, an administrator merging past a protection that wants an approval, a scheduled merge that is canceled and then does not happen, required against optional checks with `--watch`, and `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose` from a real clone. The test of the cancel showed that Gitea answers a cancel with nothing scheduled with the same bare 404 as for a missing pull request, which the code now reads as "nothing scheduled".
